s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent syncope with evidence of cardiac dysfunction and conduction abnormalities
salient_findings: Recurrent syncope over 24 hours
New left bundle branch block on ECG
Moderate-size area of inferior wall ischaemia and scar on pharmacological nuclear stress test
Prolonged QTc interval on ECG
Intermittent high-grade AV block with ventricular escape beats on telemetry
key_facts: 50-year-old man with a remote history of treated Lyme disease
No hypertension, hyperlipidemia, or diabetes
Four episodes of syncope over 24 hours
Initial workup six weeks earlier was unrevealing
New left bundle branch block on outpatient ECG
Exercise stress testing provoked presyncope with a brief burst of atrial tachycardia
LVEF of 42% with a moderate-size area of inferior wall ischaemia and scar on pharmacological nuclear stress test
No chest pain or heart failure symptoms
Vital signs: blood pressure 140/66 mmHg, heart rate 54 bpm, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, temperature 36.2°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air
Physical examination was unremarkable
12-lead ECG showed sinus rhythm at 57 bpm, first-degree AV block, and a prolonged QTc
Brief burst of atrial tachycardia that resolved with IV metoprolol
Cardiac enzymes, thyroid function tests, serum calcium, and ACE levels were normal
Lyme antibody testing was negative
Chest radiograph was normal
Transthoracic echocardiography showed an LVEF of 45–50% with no regional wall motion abnormalities
Telemetry captured intermittent high-grade AV block with ventricular escape beats

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Evidence of cardiac dysfunction and conduction abnormalities, with a low RV ejection fraction of 23%

shortlist.label: Cardiac sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of mediastinal and bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, and cardiac dysfunction

shortlist.label: Long QT syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Prolonged QTc interval on ECG, which can cause syncope and arrhythmias

shortlist.label: Progressive cardiac conduction defect
shortlist.why_kept: History of new left bundle branch block, first-degree AV block, and high-grade AV block with ventricular escape beats

shortlist.label: Dilated cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Low LVEF of 31% and evidence of cardiac dysfunction, with no clear alternative explanation

raw.rationale: The presence of mediastinal and bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy on the contrast-enhanced CT scan, along with the cardiac findings of reduced LVEF, high-grade AV block, and late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac MRI, are consistent with cardiac sarcoidosis.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The cardiac MRI showed mid-myocardial late gadolinium enhancement in the basal anteroseptal wall, which is not typical for arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy, and the right ventricular ejection fraction was low but not the primary finding.

rejected.label: Long QT syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient had a prolonged QTc, the primary clinical presentation and other findings do not align closely with Long QT syndrome, which typically presents with torsades de pointes and does not explain the full spectrum of cardiac and extracardiac findings.

rejected.label: Progressive cardiac conduction defect
rejected.why: This diagnosis does not account for the reduced LVEF, areas of ischemia and scar, or the systemic findings like lymphadenopathy.

rejected.label: Dilated cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The presence of lymphadenopathy and specific patterns of late gadolinium enhancement suggest a more specific diagnosis than dilated cardiomyopathy, which is a broader category of heart muscle disease.
